To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) buffer thrashing can severely reduce the performance of concurrent mergesorts with multiple disks and parallel prefetching and (2) buffer thrashing avoidance can be achieved through proper run placement policies that can significantly improve the performance of concurrent merging.
(1) parallel prefetching can substantially improve the performance of concurrent mergesorts, and (2) a buffer thrashing avoidance run placement policy is the best among the policies we have examined.

the best run placement policy for concurrent mergesorts is the one that places the output runs of the jobs on the same disk as at least one input run, and that the best buffer management strategy for concurrent mergesorts that use parallel prefetching is the one that uses a proper set of disks dedicated for output runs and the rest of the disk for prefetching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
buffer management in concurrent mergesorts with prefetching and with data placement for such mergesorts.

the design of buffer management and run placement policies for the merge phase in concurrent mergesorts with multiple disks, where the initial sorted runs (the inputs) are distributed among disks, and each sorted run resides only on one disk.

the following issues: (1) What is the best way to place the initial sorted runs (the input runs) of a merge job on multiple disks so that the output run of the job will be written on only one of the disks, (2) What are the best buffer management strategies for concurrent merges with parallel prefetching, and (3) How can buffer thrashing be effectively controlled for concurrent merges with prefetching?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performance for the merge phase is achieved by a run-placement policy that uses parallel prefetching of input runs and that uses buffer thrashing control to prevent buffer thrashing.
parallel prefetching with buffer thrashing avoidance and control is a very effective approach for improving the performance of concurrent mergesorts.

, in the presence of parallel prefetching, the best performance is achieved by using a proper subset of the disks dedicated for writing output runs and the rest of the disk for prefetching the initial sorted runs of a merge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the concurrent merge phase, parallel prefetching is attractive and buffer thrashing control is essential, but the best performance is achieved by using a dedicated subset of disks for writing and the remaining disks for prefetching.

the best performance for concurrent mergesort using parallel prefetching is achieved by the policy that uses a subset of disks dedicated to writing the output runs and the rest of disks used for parallel prefetching of the input runs.
the best performance is achieved when the output runs are placed on a subset of disks and the input runs are placed on another subset of disks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the run placement policy should be designed with careful buffer management in mind.
the benefits of prefetch can be maximized by using buffer thrashing avoidance and a proper run placement policy.
, for concurrent mergesorts, the best run placement policy is the one that uses buffer thrashing control to avoid thrashing, but uses parallel prefetching to reduce the average response time.
